annotations.text:
The audience side is page two.

Open the pages menu in the toolbar and pick "The audience (V2)": onboarding, the Marquee, the session page and the two prompts, the nine beats of the night, the three room layouts, the recap and the Taste Passport.

That page is what a curator's audience actually sees.
V1 is everything on this page. Five design partners get exactly this, with no audience on the other end, and two weeks to break it.

1J8 and 1J9 are new since the 6 Aug call. The promo kit is where reach becomes reservations, and its tracked links are the only way we ever learn the conversion rate the whole business turns on. The dry run is what makes a curator beta possible before an audience exists.
1J4 is the screen the product lives or dies on. Manual mm:ss never goes away. Screenshot and natural language write into it, and both can say they are not sure.
Projectionist never touches the film. No player, no rights, no integration. The whole catalogue of cinema is available on day one.

Chat handles are paper, never marquee gold: gold belongs to the pre-show and never appears mid-film. Film title and position sit on every live surface. Silver and its glow appear only where something is genuinely live.
